macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $87,000 as crypto market rallies and liquidations top $1 billion
items.summary: Bitcoin surged past $87,000 for the first time since January, while Ethereum, XRP, and Dogecoin also climbed sharply. The move coincided with more than $1 billion in crypto liquidations, mostly bearish shorts, and a jump in the global crypto market cap to about $2.91 trillion.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $85,000 on strong ETF inflows and improving risk sentiment
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered from Asian-session lows near $85,000 and traded around $86,000 as falling oil prices supported risk appetite. U.S.-listed spot bitcoin ETFs reportedly drew nearly $1 billion in inflows, their biggest single-day haul since last October.

items.title: Crypto market cap reclaims $3 trillion as altcoins join Bitcoin rally
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $86,000 while Ether, XRP, and Solana also posted gains, helping push the total crypto market back above $3 trillion. The rally was accompanied by strong momentum across major tokens and heavier trading volume.

items.title: Regulatory backdrop turns more supportive as U.S. digital asset rules advance
items.summary: Crypto markets gained alongside reports that regulators are moving through digital asset rules following the Clarity Act vote. Another report said the SEC greenlit blockchain-based versions of securities to begin trading in the U.S., boosting related tokens.

items.title: Short liquidations drive much of the crypto market’s breakout
items.summary: Multiple reports said roughly $800 million to over $1 billion in crypto positions were liquidated in the past 24 hours, with most of the forced closures coming from shorts. Bitcoin open interest also rose sharply, reinforcing the strength of the move.

items.title: Bittensor and other AI-linked tokens stand out in the day’s gains
items.summary: Beyond Bitcoin, AI-focused tokens such as Bittensor and the Artificial Superintelligence Alliance were among the strongest performers over the last 24 hours. One report also highlighted Bittensor as one of the market’s sharpest gainers.

items.title: Cardano’s x402 integration and Hyperliquid’s token burn highlight project-level developments
items.summary: Cardano reportedly joined the official x402 SDK, enabling apps and AI agents to pay in ADA over HTTP without accounts or API keys. Separately, Hyperliquid repurchased and burned about 39,980 HYPE tokens worth roughly $3.76 million over the past 24 hours.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: xAI releases Grok 4.7
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.7, describing it as its most capable model yet and highlighting improved self-verification and longer-context handling. The model is also being offered with published token pricing for input and output use.

items.title: Xiaomi opens up MiMo-V2.6 Pro and Flash
items.summary: Xiaomi debuted open-weight MiMo-V2.6 Pro and Flash multimodal models. Reports say MiMo-V2.6 Pro is performing at or near frontier-model levels on several agent benchmarks, making it a notable open-weight release.

items.title: Tencent launches Hy Image 3.5 Preview
items.summary: Tencent released Hy Image 3.5 Preview, its latest image-generation model. The company says internal testing showed results comparable to ByteDance’s Seedream 5.0 Pro.

items.title: Alibaba outlines a 5T- to 10T-parameter model push
items.summary: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the company plans to train a new model in the 5 trillion to 10 trillion parameter range. The announcement is part of a broader AI strategy spanning models, chips, and data centers.

items.title: Alibaba unveils the Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator
items.summary: Alibaba’s T-Head unit introduced the Zhenwu V900 accelerator, which it says triples the performance of its predecessor. The chip is designed to scale to very large clusters, signaling continued investment in AI infrastructure.

items.title: Meta’s Muse AI agent draws rapid adoption and security scrutiny
items.summary: Sensor Tower data shows Meta’s Muse AI agent was downloaded more than 902,000 times in its first six days, outpacing Meta AI in the same period. Separately, a researcher reported a token-access flaw in the Muse Mac app, which Meta said it hotfixed.

items.title: Shopify plans to let Muse complete purchases
items.summary: Shopify is reportedly preparing to let Meta’s Muse agent complete purchases at Shopify-powered stores through Shop Pay. If implemented broadly, this would be a notable step toward agentic commerce.

items.title: US and China discuss AI safety coordination
items.summary: News reports say US and Chinese officials discussed an AI incident-alert or safety plan ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. The talks suggest both governments are treating frontier-model risk and incident response as a diplomatic issue.

items.title: The EU proposes new data-center energy and water disclosure rules
items.summary: The European Union is proposing labeling requirements for data centers above 500 kW to disclose energy and water efficiency. The move reflects growing regulatory pressure on the infrastructure footprint of AI.

items.title: AI spending forecast rises sharply in Europe
items.summary: IDC projects European AI spending will approach $470 billion by 2030, with generative AI making up a majority share and agentic AI driving much of the growth. The forecast underscores continued enterprise demand despite broader efficiency concerns.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Xbox reportedly plans another round of layoffs and studio consolidation
items.summary: Reports say Xbox will cut hundreds of employees this week in a second major staff reduction of 2026, with several game studios also set to be consolidated. The move has triggered broader concern about additional restructuring across Microsoft’s gaming division.

items.title: Bungie says it will restore vaulted Destiny 2 content and rework Marathon
items.summary: Bungie announced plans to bring back older Destiny 2 content that had been vaulted and outlined substantial changes for Marathon. The update is one of the most significant live-service announcements of the day.

items.title: Lufia I & II: The Sinistrals Saga announced for modern platforms
items.summary: A new Lufia collection was announced for PS5, Switch 2, Switch, and PC. The reveal adds another classic RPG revival to this week’s wave of retro game announcements.

items.title: Legacy of Kain: Defiance remastered physical editions dated for November
items.summary: Physical editions of Legacy of Kain: Defiance Remastered are set to launch on November 13. The announcement continues the trend of classic action games returning in refreshed editions.

items.title: DualSense Wireless Controller LISA limited edition announced
items.summary: Sony announced a DualSense Wireless Controller LISA limited edition alongside new merchandise. The collaboration adds another major hardware-and-merchandising reveal for PlayStation fans.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts comes to Fortnite this week
items.summary: Game Informer says Kingdom Hearts content is coming to Fortnite this week. The crossover is one of the more notable game collaboration announcements in the past 24 hours.

items.title: Star Fox Adventures arrives on Nintendo Switch Online for Switch 2
items.summary: Star Fox Adventures is available via Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack on Nintendo Switch 2 today. The release brings a GameCube-era classic to Nintendo’s current subscription library.

items.title: New PlayStation Store games roll out this week
items.summary: A PlayStation Store update lists 16 new games arriving this week, including CONTROL Resonant and Demeo x Dungeons & Dragons: Battlemarked DLC. It signals a busy release window on PlayStation platforms.

items.title: Nintendo-related anniversary buzz centers on Zelda remake and Switch 2 talk
items.summary: Coverage this week highlights Zelda 40th anniversary news, including chatter about an Ocarina of Time remake and a Switch 2 console. The reports reflect strong momentum around Nintendo’s next hardware cycle.

items.title: Industry reporting points to more Xbox news and possible Halo franchise changes
items.summary: Additional reports suggest more Xbox restructuring news may be coming, with some speculation that Halo could be moved under Activision-Blizzard management. These claims remain reporting-based and not officially confirmed by Microsoft.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Google fined €403 million over GDPR location-data violations
items.summary: Ireland’s data watchdog imposed a €403 million penalty on Google for breaches involving users’ location data, making privacy enforcement the biggest non-AI tech story in the past day. The case highlights continued regulatory pressure on major platforms over data handling practices.

items.title: Google fined $463 million in EU location-data case
items.summary: AP reports that Google was fined 403 million euros for breaching EU privacy rules tied to location data, reinforcing a major regulatory development for the company. The fine is one of the most significant tech industry actions reported in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Googlebook unveiled with hardware from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo
items.summary: Google introduced Googlebook hardware with flagship devices from multiple PC makers and deep Android integration, with pricing starting at $899 and availability expected in October. This is one of the clearest major product-launch stories in the latest tech coverage.

items.title: Apple opens Apple Music Hall in London
items.summary: Apple unveiled Apple Music Hall, a new live music venue at Battersea Power Station in London with capacity for up to 600 people plus recording and mixing studios. The move expands Apple’s footprint into physical media and entertainment spaces.

items.title: Google and EU move on data-center energy and water disclosure rules
items.summary: The EU proposed labeling rules requiring large data centers to disclose energy and water efficiency, which could affect major cloud and infrastructure operators. This is a significant policy development for the broader tech industry and digital infrastructure sector.

items.title: Meta’s consumer AI agent drives tech-stock rally
items.summary: Meta’s Muse app has become a major market story, helping fuel a broader rebound in technology shares as investors rotate back into the sector. While the underlying product is AI-related, the bigger development is the market impact on tech and semiconductors.
